page: Microsoft Azure F2-1amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Allocated via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, delivering an unusually high ratio of 16 GB per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AVX512-BF16, AES, and SHA-NI. The server includes 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and operates without an attached discrete GPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded compute metrics contrasting with limited aggregate throughput due to the single-core allocation. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance scored 3551.58, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. It demonstrated similar top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 40.79 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.87 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics like the aggregate PassMark CPU score of 3401.25 and PassMark database operations of 1454.74 fall into the bottom 25 percent. Memory performance registers in the middle tier, yielding 41.76 GB/sec read and 31.4 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks.

The primary hardware tradeoff stems from combining high single-core compute frequencies and high RAM density with a strict one-core limit. While small language model inference achieves moderate throughput with 171.22 tokens/sec on a 135M model, heavier 7B model generation degrades to 5.3 tokens/sec, and static web serving reaches only 2.65 GB/sec. This architecture provides cost efficiency for memory-heavy, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight memory caching, data compression pipelines, and auxiliary microservices that demand substantial RAM and fast NVMe scratch space without requiring parallel multi-threaded compute.
description: Microsoft Azure F2-1amds_v7 is a dedicated single-core virtual machine powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 1 vCPU, 16.0 GB of memory, and 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, this instance balances a dense 16 GB-per-core ratio with advanced vector instruction support including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI. Single-threaded performance benchmarks place this machine in the top tier, achieving 40.79 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 3551.58 in stress-ng single-core tests. However, the single-core constraint limits aggregate throughput, as evidenced by lower scores in multi-core PassMark tests, database operations, and high-concurrency static web serving. Featuring no discrete GPU, the server offers efficient resource density for memory-dependent single-threaded workloads, data compression tasks, and lightweight caching setups requiring fast local disk access.
